title: EvaluateRequest
description: Wire payload sent to POST /v1-evaluate. Read by atlasent-api/supabase/functions/v1-evaluate/handler.ts. Top-level fields are flat; `context` is an opaque record passed verbatim to the rule engine. The legacy {action, agent, api_key} shape is no longer canonical — SDKs may accept it as input for backward-compat with a deprecation warning, but MUST always serialize to the wire shape described here.

actor_id.description: Identifier of the calling actor / agent (e.g. 'clinical-data-agent').

context.description: Arbitrary policy context (environment, approvals, change_window, resource IDs). Values MUST be JSON-serializable. Defaults to {} if omitted.

request_id.description: Idempotency key. Repeat calls with the same request_id replay the original decision.

shadow.description: When true, evaluation runs but no permit is issued (mode='shadow'). Used for policy testing.

explain.description: When true, the response includes the rule-engine trace under `decisionObject.explanation`.

traceparent.description: W3C Trace Context fallback when the SDK can't add the header through a signing layer.

resource_id.description: Resource the action targets (e.g. 'release:abc123'). Bound into the canonical action hash that approval artifacts cover, so an approval issued for one resource cannot authorize another.

amount.description: Optional monetary or quantity bound. Bound into the canonical action hash.

approval.description: Optional signed approval. When the action requires human approval (rule-driven OR action-type prefix per requiresHumanApproval), /v1-evaluate verifies this artifact before issuing a permit; failure denies. Schema for the artifact lives in approval-artifact.schema.json.

approval_id.description: Reference to an artifact stored server-side. Either this or `artifact` must be present.

require_approval.description: Caller assertion that this action requires verified human approval, even when the action_type heuristic does not match. Echoed onto /v1-verify-permit so the consumer can hard-deny when the permit's persisted `approval` block is missing.

operation_intent_id.description: 2026-08-13: optional caller-generated identifier for one intended organizational effect (recommended: ULID or UUIDv4 — never a content hash). Generated once by the trusted orchestrator before the first evaluate() call for that effect and presented unchanged on every re-evaluation/retry of the SAME intent (a crash-retry re-evaluates for real and gets a new decision_id, but must reuse the same operation_intent_id). Bound into the issued permit's signed claims; /v1-verify-permit cross-checks a presented value against the bound one and denies PERMIT_BINDING_MISMATCH on disagreement. Used by the consequential-operation substrate as part of operation identity (organization + provider/destination + protected action + operation_intent_id) so two independent requests with identical payloads never collide, while a genuine retry of the same intent does. Distinct from `request_id` (a single-call replay/idempotency key) and from decision_id (audit lineage only, never operation identity) — see packages/types/src/operation-intent.ts in atlasent for the full design.

actor_identity.description: 2026-10-10 (atlasent-api#3915): optional top-level actor_identity.v1 assertion for the calling actor, forwarded unchanged by SDKs (never minted or inspected client-side). Required by /v1-evaluate for the mandatory change-control action types (production.deploy, infrastructure.change, production.rollback, secret.configuration.change): without one the runtime denies ACTOR_UNVERIFIED before any policy runs. Never nested under `context`.

environment.description: Deployment environment where the action executes (e.g. 'production', 'staging'). Bound into the permit and used for enforcement-posture lookups.

resource.description: Structured resource descriptor. Mutually exclusive with `resource_id` (prefer this form for new callers).

id.description: Instance identifier within the resource class.

current_state.description: Snapshot of the resource before the proposed action executes. Enables policy rules that reason about state transitions.

proposed_state.description: Desired state of the resource after the action executes.

execution_binding.description: Identifies the execution surface where the action will run (CI/CD adapter, DB driver, etc.). Bound into the permit for verifier-side binding checks.

execution_payload_hash.description: SHA-256 digest of the exact payload this action will execute, as BARE 64-character lowercase hex. Bound into the signed permit's `execution_hash_expected`, which is what makes PAYLOAD_MISMATCH a real check at verify time. TWO PROPERTIES ARE LOAD-BEARING, and a violation of either is DROPPED, not rejected, on the ordinary-action path — allow, permit, 200, no error anywhere: (1) BARE hex — a `sha256:` prefix fails the runtime's /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i test; (2) TOP LEVEL — the runtime destructures it from the body ALONGSIDE `context`, never from within it, so a copy nested under `context` is never a binding. Omitted, the permit is bound to the runtime's own hash of the whole request body instead, which a caller's payload digest can never equal — so re-presenting one at verify yields a deterministic mismatch on every call, and presenting nothing on a non-production permit passes with no payload check at all. The four mandatory-change-control action types and any class declaring `material_execution_fields` REJECT a caller digest with a deny instead of dropping it. As of atlasent-api#3355 the response carries `execution_payload_hash_accepted` so a caller can tell. See atlasent-api's CLAUDE.md, "A caller-supplied `execution_payload_hash` is DROPPED, not rejected".

desired_state.description: The desired end-state the actor wants the resource to reach.

fingerprint.description: Deterministic hash of the desired state (e.g. expected schema fingerprint after migration).

completion_proofs.description: Multi-actor quorum completion proofs. Each entry asserts that a specific actor consumed a specific permit for a specific action_type. The runtime verifies both the permit_uses consumed-gate and an execution_evaluations actor/action binding gate before counting the proof toward quorum.

state_snapshot.description: State snapshot of the system at evaluation time. Required when the action class has requires_state_snapshot=true (enforced by migration 20260603000019). Omitting this field on a required action class causes the server to return decision=deny with deny_code=SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED. Recovery: add state_snapshot to every evaluate call for the affected action_type.

source_kind.description: Classification of the source. 'trusted' for verified systems, 'untrusted' for caller-provided snapshots.

complete.description: Whether the snapshot is complete. false when only a partial view is available.

payload.description: Arbitrary snapshot payload — observable state of the system at evaluation time.

evaluation_profile.description: Controls which algorithm layers run. 'basic' skips snapshot enforcement (pilot-safe). 'standard' is the default and applies all stable layers. 'advanced'/'enterprise' enable override logic and additional authority checks. Unknown values fall back to 'standard' server-side.

override.description: Emergency override block. Only evaluated when evaluation_profile is 'advanced' or 'enterprise'. Allows an authorised operator (holding override:execute scope) to accept snapshot hard blocks with explicit justification. The operator must differ from the requester (no self-approval).

authority_actor_id.description: Actor ID of the operator authorising this override. Must differ from the requester's actor_id. Must hold override:execute scope on an active API key in the org.

reason.description: Mandatory human-readable justification. Stored verbatim in the CDO and audit event.

time_bound_seconds.description: Override validity window in seconds. Defaults to 900 (15 min). Capped at 3600 (1 hour).

incident_id.description: Incident or change ticket ID. Required when state_snapshot.incident_active is true.

accepted_blocks.description: Explicit list of snapshot hard-block codes this override accepts. When present, any block NOT in this list is still a hard deny.
